items.q: What makes a conversation effortful vs effortless?
items.a: Effortful = small-talk land, hunting the next line, unspoken awkwardness. Effortless = flow, never empty, a little sad when it ends. Vinh: the gap is **subtext listening**, not charm.

items.q: What do most people listen to, and what do they miss?
items.a: Only the **text** — the words. Every talk also leaks through **voice, body, and emotion**. Miss those and you have no threads to pull.

items.q: What are the four channels of subtext listening?
items.a: **Brain** = word choice ("depleted" ≠ "tired"). **Ears** = vocal change (pause, quieter "fine"). **Eyes** = body. **Heart** = emotion. Heart is last — you infer it from a **cluster** of the first three.
Any four-channel cue that **deviates from that person's norm**. Stoic says "rattled." Bubbly voice goes flat. Upright person slumps. Not a generic cue dictionary.

items.q: After you notice a thread, what do you actually say?
items.a: **Reflect one** — their exact words or one body/voice notice. Not the whole cluster. Not Sherlock. "Pissed off? How so?" Wrong emotion-guess is useful: they correct you.

items.q: What do you do right after you reflect?
items.a: **Shut up.** Hold space. Depth needs time. Hijacking with your own story kills the thread. Then **pull** the next one they just dropped.

items.q: How do you share without turning it into an interrogation — or advice?
items.a: **They share three, you share one.** Share **experience, not advice**. If unsure: "Do you want me to try to help or do you just want me to listen?"
